newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB extends gains on digital TV hopes.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB extends gains on digital TV hopes.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc rose sharply for a second day on Thursday as the market continued to respond eagerly to the company's digital TV plans, dealers and analysts said .

The stock was up 13-1/2p at 636-1/2 by 0853 GMT, its highest level in over three months, after yesterday rising 30p. Trading volume was an active 1.6 million shares, making it the third most active stock in the UK market.
"This is a stock that tends to be driven very heavily by sentiment and sentiment is running very positively at the moment," said Richard Dale, analyst at Salomon Brothers.
On Wednesday BSkyB laid out plans for an Autumn launch of its 200-channel digital satellite service, opening the way to a significant expansion of potentially lucrative pay-per-view channels.
It also said it remained optimistic about prospects for digital television in Germany, where it has been in talks for seven months on taking a stake in Kirch Gruppe's DF1.
Dale said it was the prospects for digital TV in the UK and Germany that was driving the stock.

"I think it is a combination of the positive outlook in terms of digital terrestrial television, and a growing appreciation of the benefits the company will get from that, and hopes for a resolution on DF1," the Salomon analyst said.
